data.name: Srikant
data.gender_notes: Srikant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the Lord of all wealth, including material and spiritual wealth. The name Srikant carries the meaning “Lord of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Srikant usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for Lord Vishnu, signifying the abundance of wealth, both material and spiritual.
data.etymology: Srikant belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Srikant total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_sanskrit.name: श्रीकान्त
in_sanskrit.meaning: Wealthy, prosperous, and possessed of the Goddess of Fortune
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: श्री (Shri) - Wealthy, prosperous, abundant कान्त (Kant) - Possessed of, belonging to, God of desire (Kama Deva) or Goddess of Fortune (Lakshmi)

in_hindi.name: श्रीकान्त
in_hindi.meaning: श्री (Shri) - वेदिक शक्ति, धन, सुख, प्रसाद (Wealth, prosperity, power, grace, blessings) कान्त (Kant) - कामदेव के साथियों से संगत, या लक्ष्मी के साथिय (Belonging to, associated with, God of desire Kama Deva or Goddess of Fortune Lakshmi)

in_tamil.name: ஶ்ரீகாந்த
in_tamil.meaning: ஶ்ரீ (Shri) - ஆனந்தும் வெள்ளியால், வெளியிட்டும் வளர்ந்தும் (Wealth, prosperity, power, grace) காந்த (Kant) - காமம் அல்லது லக்ஷ்மியிட்டு இடம் களிய (Belonging to, associated with, God of desire Kamadeva or Goddess of Fortune Lakshmi)

in_telugu.name: శ్రీకాంట
in_telugu.meaning: శ్రీ (Shri) - దేశియోద్యే, దేశియోద్యేశ్వరయోద్యే, శుభదేశయోద్యే (Wealth, prosperity, power, grace, blessings) కాంట (Kant) - కామదేశయోద్యేయ సహోదరయోద్యే, లక్ష్మీయోద్యేయ సహోదరయోద్యే (Belonging to, associated with, God of desire Kamadeva or Goddess of Fortune Lakshmi)

in_marathi.name: Srikant
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Lord of Wealth
in_marathi.long_meaning: Srikant हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। One who is the Lord of all wealth, including material and spiritual wealth.

in_bengali.name: Srikant
in_bengali.meaning: হিন্দু নাম যার অর্থ Lord of Wealth
in_bengali.long_meaning: Srikant একটি হিন্দু নাম যা ভারতীয় সংস্কৃতিতে গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক তাৎপর্য রাখে। One who is the Lord of all wealth, including material and spiritual wealth.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the name Srikant holds deep reverence and respect as it is associated with the divine aspect of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and fortune. Srikant is considered to be the one who is blessed with the wealth and prosperity bestowed by Lakshmi, signifying material wealth as well as inner happiness and contentment. In social and familial contexts, the name Srikant is often linked to success, power, and good fortune.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Srikant signifies the supreme Lord, who holds the power to grant wealth in its truest form. It is believed that those named Srikant have a deep connection with the divine, and are blessed with the abundance of Lakshmi's grace. This name reminds us of the ultimate goal of seeking material and spiritual wealth, and striving for a balanced and virtuous life, devoted to the attainment of inner happiness and external prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Srikant, derived from Sanskrit, means 'God's great joy'. It symbolizes the joy and bliss experienced when one's life is dedicated to the divine. The name is a reminder to always seek the divine in all aspects of life, cultivating happiness, peace, and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Srikanta, also known as Bhagavat Tirtha, was a prominent Dvaita philosopher and a direct disciple of Madhvacharya. He is considered the founder of the sub-school of Dvaita known as 'Srivaishnavism'. He lived between 1296 and 1386 AD.
historical_references.context: Philosopher and founder of Srivaishnavism sub-school of Dvaita philosophy

historical_references.reference: Srikanta, also known as Srikanta Sastri, was a renowned 19th century Hindu scholar and scholarly editor of the Sanskrit works of Ramanuja. He was born in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu in 1824 and spent most of his life in Tirupati. He was a great exponent of the Shankara-Madhva-Ramanuja triad and authored several works on the Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana, and other scriptures.
historical_references.context: Hindu scholar and scholarly editor of Sanskrit works
